momentum. Customers continue to adopt Microsoft 365 Copilot at a faster rate than any other

Now, let's turn to applications and agents we ourselves are building on this platform. We now
have 900 million monthly active users of our AI features across our products. And our first-party
family of Copilots now has surpassed 150 million monthly active users across information work,
coding, security, science, health and consumer. When it comes to information work, we continue
to innovate with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Copilot is becoming the UI for the agentic AI experience. We have integrated chat and agentic workflows into everyday tools like Outlook, Word, Excel,
PowerPoint and Teams. Just nine months since release, tens of millions of users across Microsoft
365 customer base are already using chat. Adoption is accelerating rapidly, growing 50% quarter-
over-quarter and we continue to see usage intensity increase. This quarter, we also introduced
Agent Mode, which turns single prompts into expert quality Word Documents, Excel
Spreadsheets, PowerPoint Presentation and then iterate to deliver the final product, much like
Agent Mode in coding tools today. We're thrilled by the early response, including third-party
benchmarks that rank it best-in-class. Beyond individual productivity, Copilot is multi-player with Teams Mode announced this week. You
can now invite colleagues into a Copilot conversation. And our collaborative agents like Facilitator
and Project Manager prep meeting agendas, take notes, capture decision, kick-off group tasks.

Bull Case/PT
Core Azure growth accelerates further, and MSFT’s GenAI contribution becomes stronger
and more diversified via faster adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, and
Security Copilot. Impressive operating margin expansion persists even as the company
invests in key growth areas (GenAI, Fabric, etc. ). Our bull case valuation utilizes a
CY26-27E P/E multiple of 40x and 33x, equating to $700. Bear Case/PT
Core Azure growth decelerates more than expected due to increasing competition, an
execution misstep and/or a worsening macro environment. Adoption of GenAI offerings
shows signs of plateauing after the initial adoption wave. Operating margins are lower
than expected, as MSFT cannot remotely offset investments that increasingly impact the
model. Our bear case valuation utilizes a CY26-27E P/E multiple of 24x and 20x, equating
to $420. Risks
Core consumption growth decelerates more than anticipated as macro challenges
resurface. Competition among cloud infrastructure providers materially increases, leading
to pricing pressure. GenAI adoption and monetization is slower than expected. Azure
suffers a significant breach, triggering churn and a loss of customer confidence. MSFT
fails to anticipate and adapt to evolving technology trends. Global PC shipments slow and
the “AI PC” era does not in fact help MSFT. Ongoing success and dominance across a
range of enterprise markets globally prompts increased regulatory scrutiny.

We also
note the launch of Wave 3 for MSFT Copilot which includes the offering of Anthropic's models
(beside OpenAI) and Claude Cowork capabilities and cements MSFT's role as a successful fast
follower of new technology. When MSFT launched Copilot a while ago, many investors asked why it was not part of a new
SKU (E7 for example). At the time, it seemed MSFT wanted to make Copilot available to a
broader audience (not just the high-end SKU customers) and hence the separate pricing. However, it does create friction in the sales process, especially for the enterprise level, if two
different pricing agreements (an Office SKU and the Copilot commitment) and discount levels
need to be discussed. In this respect, the new E7 offerings is just a natural extension. E7 includes
E5 plus Copilot and Agent 365. At $99 per user, the offering is above the $60 E5 price (price
update on July 2026) but is cheaper than the individual components (E5 $60 plus Copilot $30
plus Agent 365 $15). We note that in recent quarters, E5 was mentioned as the main growth
driver for Office growth, followed by Copilot. With its product announcements today, Microsoft also provides an answer for another recent
investor discussion point around the evolution of work.
[25] <20260205_Mizuho_Securities_MSFT_MSFT-_Good_O | grep>
More specifically, this includes the incremental
$250B in Azure commitments from the recent OpenAI agreement. Despite continued high capex, reported gross margins were very good at 68. 0%, easily above our
67. 0% target and the Street's ~67. 1% forecast. Further, OMs of 47. 1% were much better than
expected and easily surpassed our and the Street's 45. 3% target. In addition, under the equity
method of accounting, OpenAI contributed a $9. 978B gain (vs. a $4. 061B loss previously) to Other
Income & Expense (OI&E), and a $7. 583B net gain (vs. $3. 086B net loss previously). Non-GAAP
EPS - excluding this component - was $4. 14 vs. our $3. 96 estimate and the Street's $3. 91 forecast. Finally, CFFO of $35. 8B came in well above the Street's $30. 4B estimate. Good Azure Performance, But With Allocations Constraining Growth Somewhat
As noted above, Azure revenue growth of 38% Y/Y CC, which exceeded mgmt's guidance that
had called for 37% growth Y/Y, although this did come in slightly below buy-side expectations. This was also slightly below the 39% growth rate reported in F1Q. Having said that, mgmt did also
indicate that having to allocate additional GPU capacity to certain first-party applications (such
as Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot), as well as to R&D and further product innovation,
weighed on Azure growth this quarter by at least a couple of points.

In security, our end-to-end stack is now informed by
100 trillion daily signals, 1 billion monthly active users of Entra, 16 billion Copilot interactions
audited by Purview, up 72% quarter-over-quarter, 40,000 sentinel customers and we took share
across all categories we serve in security. In LinkedIn, nearly 1. 3 billion members. And finally, in gaming, we expanded our reach across every
endpoint focused on our high margin content and services. We launched critically acclaimed
games like Keeper, Ninja Gaiden 4 and Outer Worlds 2, reaching 155 million monthly active users
in Minecraft, an all-time high and set new record for overall content and services revenue for the
quarter. We also saw a great response to Xbox Ally launch two weeks ago and set new records
for players on PC. In closing, our planet-scale Cloud and AI factory together with Copilots across high-value domains
is driving broad diffusion and real-world impact, and we continue to increase our investments in AI
across both capital and talent to meet the massive opportunity ahead. With that, let me turn it over to Amy to walk through our financial results and outlook, and I look
forward to rejoining for your questions. Amy Hood {BIO 18040963 <GO>}
Thank you, Satya, and good afternoon, everyone. First, as you heard from Satya, we were
pleased to announce the next phase of our partnership with OpenAI yesterday.
[27] <Microsoft_Corp_Earnings_Call_2026128_RT00000 | grep>
Today, I'll focus my remarks across the three layers of our stack, cloud and
token factory, Agent platform, and high-value agentic experiences. When it comes to our cloud and token factory, the key to long-term competitiveness is shaping
our infrastructure to support new high-scale workloads. We're building this infrastructure out for
the heterogeneous and distributed nature of these workloads, ensuring the right fit with the
geographic and segment-specific needs for all customers, including the long tail. The key metric
we're optimizing for is tokens per watt per dollar, which comes down to increasing utilization and
decreasing TCO using silicon, systems, and software. A good example of this is the 50% increase in throughput we were able to achieve in one of our
highest volume workloads, OpenAI inferencing, powering our Copilots. And another example was
the unlocking of new capabilities and efficiencies for our Fairwater data centers. In this instance,
we connected both Atlanta and Wisconsin site through an AI WAN to build a first-of-its-kind AI
super factory. Fairwater's two-story design and liquid cooling allow us to run higher GPU densities
and thereby improve both performance and latencies for high-scale training. All up, we added nearly 1 gigawatt of total capacity this quarter alone. At the silicon layer, we have
NVIDIA and AMD and our own Maia chips delivering the best all-up fleet performance, cost, and
supply across multiple generations of hardware.
